paragraphs: Hart InterCivic sells voting systems and election services to the officials who run elections. In one configuration, voters mark a paper ballot with a pen and the ballot is scanned to capture the vote digitally. A hybrid option combines touchscreen voting with a voter-verifiable paper trail. Absentee and mail ballots are handled through central scanning.

On the paper-based products, voter choices are never encoded in a digital seal for tabulation. Products carry role-based controls meant to keep an election transparent end to end. The company announced certification of a newer product line, Vanguard, to the VVSG 2.0 standard by the Election Assistance Commission. Within that line, Flex is a universal ballot marking device. Vault handles the scanning of ballots, whether marked by hand or by machine. Workspace covers end-to-end election management.

Hart says it has worked side by side with election professionals for more than 100 years. Its regional offices span coast to coast. The company also states that Vanguard is the only voting system available in the United States that delivers on both the latest EAC standard and the conditions of the executive order it cites.
